summary: The corpus supports one broad happen/befall sense. Harm under negation or prediction follows from the event and context; do not split a separate harm sense from mede or zyono. Affected participants occur as b-/e- phrases, l-suffixes, or b-rišo/b-qarʕo; an overt affected participant need not be expressed.

Plural event descriptions often accompany singular-shaped ǧari/ǧore (MAC Hanna Dewo/89, /102; MAC Ishaq Material culture/32). 29/174 and 29/180 have feminine ǧaryo. These facts warrant an agreement study, not a global claim that the verb is invariant.
Preterit-wa ǧariwaylux is explicit at 110/21. -lux beside feminine aʕlax/xoṯax is preserved. Infectum-wa ranges over habitual past and echo questions; the plain event meaning is unchanged.
24/301 has ʕade ǧari yo aʕmi. The proposed gloss mentioned ʕal-, but the actual phrase uses aʕmi. It may contain borrowed adjectival ǧāri; no new finite sense is published.

94/359 miǧaryo is paraphrased by mitəštaʕyo and denotes a game’s execution. This is real evidence for a derived Detransitive construction, but III versus II and base forms could not be determined from this input. It does not belong to ǧry2 dare.
Məǧ-ǧarila at MAC NE Sterka Zera/24 does not securely establish ko-Preterit; interrogative mə plus plain Preterit remains possible.
The inherited PrS quotations align with PrS 26/28 and 75/96 despite page-style references prs 64/10 and prs 221/5; no citation correction is justified merely by the different reference systems.

All seven compact occurrences initially lacking verses were recovered and checked in inputs/texts. MAC Murder in Kfarze, Interview with Numan/1 explicitly has plural ǧarən with Hani kulle; the verb is therefore not invariably singular. At 65/163 the two tokens occur in a comparison; at 113/85 ebux is second person, correcting the reader’s paraphrase.
Confirm the segmentation/vowel of Məǧ-ǧarila at MAC NE Sterka Zera/24 before adding ko-Preterit.
Is 24/301 ǧari a finite Turoyo form or borrowed adjective ǧāri, and what explains the agreement with ʕade?
For 94/359 miǧaryo, establish II versus III and attested base forms before creating a stem. Its execution meaning is supported by the parallel mitəštaʕyo.
Check -lux with feminine address at 110/21; -lux versus German mir at 52/187; repeated ebe buwe at PrS 30/40; and the referent of ǧəralle at Talay 2/20.
Inanimate affectees include cheese, grain, lime mortar, clothing and books. The event remains subject (often mede); the affected entity is l-marked, not a transitive agent.
b-rišo and b-qarʕo are body-part variants of already attested affected-person coding, not separate experience senses.
